Scope and entry details

Include protection, surface preparation, dust control, disposal, repairs, filling, grinding, compatible primer, joint treatment and curing. Quote concrete repairs, floor prep, or both; identify your scope.

Do not place a thin concrete layer over the whole slab. Use concrete only for deep repairs that can accept it. Leave about ¼–½″ for precision material above deep repairs where practical; this is not a minimum coat elsewhere.

The front uses the current −17.11 mm prepared-edge pricing basis, pending confirmation of the mall reference. Final tile tie-in, doors and slope require coordination. The flooring is 12.5 mm wood plus adhesive. Wood installation and entry-tile work are separate; price moisture mitigation separately pending testing.

These are bid targets, not released setting-out instructions. Confirm field conditions, access, work hours and product system with LBCo.

Map numbers = added millimetres. G = grinding. Purple ring = repair first. Click for inches.

How the map is calculated

Each square uses one reading from the 4-foot survey grid. Targets are +21 mm in the red area and door triangle, and change along the slopes. Fill is target minus existing elevation; holes use the assumed repaired surface. At target: no work. Above target: grind the excess.

Quantities account for boundaries and slopes within each grid area. This map does not show every small hump or hole; repair sizes need field checks. The front retains the conditional −17.11 mm target used for pricing.
